topic: Devils Hole and the distant Kamchatka earthquake
centralQuestion: How did an earthquake thousands of miles away make waves in a Nevada desert cave?
thesis: Passing seismic motion can set local enclosed water oscillating; a modest physical disturbance can affect the shallow shelf of an apparently isolated habitat.
viewerPayoff: Explain the distant-earthquake/local-water connection and its limited, real ecological consequence.

sources.organization: National Park Service / Death Valley National Park
sources.title: Russian earthquake causes minor disturbance in Devils Hole
sources.notes: Direct site-operator event report and biological interpretation. Authoritative for local observations, not an independent analysis of raw monitoring data. Distance, delay and wave size are reported NPS values. Amplitude convention and raw onset series are absent; no universal seismic speed is derived. December/February ecological effects and the March count of 38 fish are separate observations and unused. The before image bears July 14, 2025; the after image July 30. They are not immediately adjacent observations or a quantitative mortality comparison.

sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey / Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.title: Seismic Seiches
sources.notes: Established mechanism from the relevant scientific agency. A different institution from NPS, not independent replication of July 2025 cave monitoring. General physics, not a calculated Devils Hole normal mode, calibrated amplitude or exact propagation path. No one-path model or claim that distance alone determines local wave height.

sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey / Earthquake Hazards Program
sources.title: Cool Earthquake Facts
sources.notes: Relevant official explanation for qualitative ground-water coupling and pronunciation. Only the bounded passage is used; volatile facts elsewhere on the page are unused. The shaken bathtub is a labeled analogy, not a measured simulation of cave displacement or frequency. Magnitude does not imply identical shaking in Russia and Nevada.

sources.organization: National Park Service / Death Valley National Park
sources.title: Devils Hole
sources.notes: Site-operator ecological and geographic context. Related to the event report, not counted as independent replication. Older temperature, population and isolation-age wording is unused. Generic two-metre waves do not describe July 2025. An unmapped bottom does not mean bottomless. Full cave geometry is unknown; show only an illustrative near-surface cutaway.

sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey / reviewed ComCat event record
sources.title: M8.8 — 2025 Kamchatka Peninsula, Russia Earthquake, us6000qw60
sources.notes: Direct USGS scientific-catalog HTTP GeoJSON response, with exact bytes preserved. Corroborates magnitude and origin date, not local wave size or delay. Current reviewed catalog metadata may differ from initial news estimates; no older epicenter or depth estimate is reused. Do not manufacture an exact cave-disturbance timestamp from the reported 21-minute interval. Calendar conversions are labeled derivations, not independent timestamp observations.

caveats.statement: Reported event values remain qualified. Energy travels through/along Earth; local water oscillates. Ten-inch July 2025 waves and minor shelf disturbance, not an ocean tsunami reaching Nevada, a two-metre wall of water, near-extinction or a current fish count. Cave/ground-motion illustrations are schematic, not measured data or footage.
